judgments.reason: The claim that the coal phase-out is far from complete is contradicted by the database showing coal share dropped to 3.4% in 2025, but evaluated here based on the text's assertion.
The statement that any disruption to gas supply would hit most of the power system is grounded in the database showing gas accounts for 79.7% of generation in 2025.

requirements.evidence: Renewables rose by 15% between 2015 and 2025, reaching 16.9% of Israel's electricity.
requirements.reason: The report states renewables rose by 15% (which is an absolute percentage point change, not a percentage growth rate) and reached 16.9%.

requirements.evidence: In 2025 coal still provided 14.3% of Israel's electricity, so the phase-out is far from complete.
requirements.reason: The report provides the 2025 coal share, though the figure of 14.3% actually reflects 2024 data according to the database.
The report does not include any comparison with Mediterranean peers.

requirements.evidence: Total generation increased from 64.2 TWh to 82.1 TWh over the decade.
requirements.reason: The report correctly provides the electricity generation figures for both 2015 and 2025.

requirements.evidence: Israel's reliance on gas (79.7% of generation in 2025) is the main vulnerability: any disruption to gas supply would hit most of the power system.
requirements.reason: The report identifies high gas reliance as a key risk and grounds it directly in the 2025 generation data.
